sub.zh: 大卫与歌利亚 · 撒母耳记上 17 章

text.en: A dusty man in a scribe's robe stands at your shoulder. His name is Corin, and he will walk this road with you.
text.zh: 一个满身风尘、穿文士长袍的人在你身边站定。他叫柯林，此后一路与你同行。

text.en: “Around 1020 BC. The Valley of Elah,” he says quietly.
text.zh: 「公元前一〇二〇年左右，以拉谷。」他低声说。

text.en: “Remember: we are only witnesses. We cannot change the ending God has written.”
text.zh: 「记住：我们只是见证人，改不了神写下的结局。」

text.en: “What we decide is what kind of people we become.”
text.zh: 「能决定的，是我们自己成为怎样的人。」

text.en: Across the valley the Philistine army has been shouting for forty days. Not one Israelite has gone out.
text.zh: 山谷对面，非利士人的军队已经骂阵四十天。四十天里，以色列没有一个人出去应战。

text.en: “So. Where will you stand?”
text.zh: 「所以，你要站在哪里？」

text.en: “The book keeps its own hours. When it opens, walk into it.”
text.zh: 「书卷自有它的时辰。它翻开的时候，走进去就是了。」

text.en: He holds his spear with both hands and does not look up.
text.zh: 他两只手抱着矛，不敢抬头。

text.en: “They say he is three metres tall. All bronze. His spear shaft is like a weaver's beam.”
text.zh: 「他们说他身高近三米，全身铜甲，枪杆粗得像织布的机轴。」

text.en: “I cannot tell. I have never been close enough to look.”
text.zh: 「我看不清。我从来没走近过。」

text.en: “The day I left, my mother told me not to be afraid.”
text.zh: 「我出门那天，我妈说不要怕。」

text.en: “Then she cried anyway. She was afraid too, and she still said it.”
text.zh: 「说完，她还是哭了。她自己也在怕，可她还是说了。」

text.en: “The officers say to the people: do not be fainthearted, do not be afraid, for the LORD your God goes with you.”
text.zh: 「官长又要对百姓说：你们不要胆怯，不要惧怕他们，因为耶和华你们的神与你们同去。」

text.en: He puts the words into your hand.
text.zh: 他把这句话交给你。

text.en: “They are not mine to keep.”
text.zh: 「它不是我的。」

text.en: “Go on up. I will hold the line here. Somebody has to.”
text.zh: 「你上去吧。这里我守着。总得有人守着。」

text.en: She breaks bread without lifting her eyes.
text.zh: 她低着头分饼，没有抬眼。

text.en: “You are going up too, then. My man went up. He has not come down.”
text.zh: 「你也要上去。我男人上去了，还没下来。」

text.en: “I do not pray that he wins,” she says.
text.zh: 「我不祷告他打赢。」她说。

text.en: “I pray he does not lose himself up there.”
text.zh: 「我祷告他别把自己丢在上面。」

text.en: “Take this. Bread, and a verse with it.”
text.zh: 「拿着。饼，还有一句诗。」

text.en: “Bread does not carry far. The words might carry you further.”
text.zh: 「饼走不了多远，这句话也许可以陪你走远一点。」

text.en: “Eat before you go up. Nobody fights well hungry.”
text.zh: 「上去之前吃点东西。饿着的人打不好仗。」

text.en: An old man sits on a stone by the road, mending a strap.
text.zh: 一个老人坐在路边的石头上修皮带。

text.en: “They will not let you through. Even the king says it: you cannot go and fight him, you are too young, he has been a fighting man since his youth.”
text.zh: 「他们不会让你过去的。连王都这么说：你不能去与那非利士人交战，因为你年纪太轻，他从小就作战士。」

text.en: “He is right that you are young. I will give him that.”
text.zh: 「他说你年轻，这话不错。」

text.en: “He is wrong to think youth is the same as useless.”
text.zh: 「他错在以为年轻就没有用。」

text.en: “I have been looked over my whole life,” he says.
text.zh: 「我这一辈子都在被人打量。」

text.en: He pulls the strap tight.
text.zh: 他把皮带拉紧。

text.en: “Carry the sentence that answers it.”
text.zh: 「把能回这句话的那一句带上。」

text.en: “The stones are at the brook, downstream past the tents. He took five. Not six.”
text.zh: 「石子在下游的溪边，过了帐篷就是。他当时捡了五块。不是六块。」

text.en: “Fear not, stand still, and see the salvation of the LORD.”
text.zh: 「你们不要胆怯，不要惧怕他们，因为耶和华你们的神与你们同去。」

text.en: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD.”
text.zh: 「你来攻击我，是靠刀枪和盾牌；我来攻击你，是靠万军之耶和华的名。」

text.en: “Man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.”
text.zh: 「耶和华不像人看人：人是看外貌，耶和华是看内心。」

text.en: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.”
text.zh: 「耶和华是我的牧者，我必不致缺乏。」

line.en: “Choose you a man, and let him come down to me!”
line.zh: 「你们拣选一个人，叫他下来到我这里来！他若能与我交战，把我杀了，我们就作你们的仆人。」

tell.en: He is shouting for the whole valley to hear. He wants you to count the distance.
tell.zh: 他喊得整条山谷都听见。他要你先数一数自己离他有多远。

line.en: “Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves?”
line.zh: 「我岂是狗呢，你竟拿杖到我这里来？」

tell.en: He is looking at your hands, and finding them empty.
tell.zh: 他在看你的手，看你手里到底有没有东西。

line.en: “Whose son is this youth? He is but a boy.”
line.zh: 「这少年人是谁的儿子？」他不再对你说话，开始对别人说你。

tell.en: He is not talking to you now. He is talking about you, to everyone else.
tell.zh: 他在跟别人说你。整座山谷都在听。

line.en: “Forty days, and thy God has sent no one. Will he save thee?”
line.zh: 「我今日向以色列人的军队骂阵。你们叫一个人出来，与我交战吧！」

tell.en: This one is quiet. It is the one that has been working all along.
tell.zh: 这一句很轻。它已经在你心里响了四十天。

triggers.note: crossing north of this row with five stones begins the BECOME

text.en: You reach the line, and your hand closes on an empty pouch. Five stones. The brook is behind you.
text.zh: 你走到界线前，手在袋子里摸了个空。要五块石子。溪水在你身后。

text.en: The brook runs low and slow where the reeds are. Smooth stones lie in it, and they will wait for you.
text.zh: 溪水又浅又凉，从谷底穿过。石子就躺在石缝里，它们会等你。

text.en: The line in the dust is still there, and your hand still knows the weight of five stones. You do not have to fight him again. You only have to remember that you stood here.
text.zh: 土里的那条界线还在，你的手还记得五块石子的重量。石子虽不是你亲手甩出的，但你真正学会的，是不再只盯着眼前的巨人。

text.en: 1 Samuel 17:47 — “And all this assembly shall know that the LORD saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’s, and he will give you into our hands.”
text.zh: 撒母耳记上 17:47 ——「又使这众人知道耶和华使人得胜，不是用刀用枪，因为争战的胜败全在乎耶和华。他必将你们交在我们手里。」

text.en: The Valley of Elah. Two armies on two hills, and a brook running between them. You are walking it as a shepherd boy named David, but the hands are yours.
text.zh: 书卷在你手里发烫，墨迹像水一样流动。营火一盏一盏亮起来，尘土和羊群的气味扑到脸上。

text.en: Left thumb moves you. Right side: A talks to whoever you face, » confirms. On a keyboard, arrows or WASD, Z to talk, X to step back.
text.zh: 左手拇指推着走。右下两个键：A 和面前的人说话，» 按住疾走。用键盘就是方向键或 WASD，Z 说话，按住 Shift 疾走。

text.en: Four people are waiting on this road. Listen to each of them, pick up what the brook is holding, and then walk north past the line in the dust.
text.zh: 有人在你身边站定，是个满身风尘、穿文士长袍的人。他叫柯林，此后一路与你同行。这条路上还有三个人在等你，把溪水里的东西捡起来，再往北走过尘土里那条界线。
